How your data is stored and searched If you arrived here from a note about your search layer
filling up, this is the full explanation behind it — no architecture required. Everything you save
is kept Your data is kept in a Postgres database. Postgres is ordinary, inexpensive storage, so we
can keep all of it. This copy is your record — the durable one: nothing is taken out of it to make
room in the fast layer. A second copy, for the things you use most On top of the record we run a
graph database. It mirrors a slice of your data in a shape that makes two things quick: finding
things by meaning rather than by exact wording, and following the connections between them — so a
search can bring back what is related to what you asked for, not only what matches it. That graph
database is expensive to run and holds far less than the record does, so it is reserved for what
matters most: the items you search for and use most often, and the items that other things hang
off. Everything else stays in the record. What happens when the fast layer fills Nothing is lost,
and nothing is deleted. Everything you have saved stays searchable. What changes is how quickly
some older items come back. When the fast layer is full, the items used least step out of it and
stay in the record. Search keeps working across everything: items outside the fast layer are
fetched when you search for them, so they can take a moment longer to answer. That is the whole
effect — you can lose speed on the items you use least; you never lose the items. What can be done
about it Add capacity. More fast capacity can be added to your account at any time — write to
hello@premiselabs.co. This makes the fast layer bigger; it is not a different plan. Keep this
resident. The things you rely on can be kept in the fast layer, together with the things connected
to them, so they do not have to be fetched back when you return to them. Keeping things resident
has a limit, so it can never take over the fast layer. See what is outside. What has stepped out
of the fast layer can be listed — how much of it, roughly when, and what it was about — so what is
outside is something you can look at rather than a black box. All three act on the fast layer,
never on your record. None of them deletes anything: whatever you choose, everything you have
saved is still there.
